item.text:
## 1B.7 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** The 2024 record leans **favorable**. Marcos appears to have relied on **formal institutions and technical/security channels** rather than openly surrounding security decisions with ideologues. The strongest evidence is the **NSC reorganization**, which explicitly centers cabinet, congressional, military, intelligence, and foreign-affairs roles. I did **not** find direct evidence of a loyalist/ideologue capture of nuclear or security decision-making in 2024.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [Executive Order No. 81](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html) — Lawphil / Office of the President, Dec. 30, 2024 | Marcos reorganized the National Security Council to make it a “resilient national security institution” and to improve coordination on national security. The membership includes cabinet, legislative, military, intelligence, and legal offices, which is strong evidence of institutional rather than purely loyalist security governance. | `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.4` |
| E2 | Favorable | [National Security Council](https://nsc.gov.ph/) — National Security Council of the Philippines, accessed 2026 | The NSC describes itself as the principal advisory body for national security, with a permanent Secretariat that provides technical support and a Director General / National Security Adviser. That supports a reading that Marcos’s security decisions were embedded in expert institutions, not ad hoc personal circles. | `1B.7`, `1B.3` |
| E3 | Favorable | [President Marcos appoints new envoys, officials](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1230426) — Philippine News Agency, Aug. 3, 2024 | Marcos added formal officials across the bureaucracy, including an assistant director general of the NSC and a special envoy on transnational crimes. This is not proof of expertise-centered decision-making by itself, but it is consistent with staffing security-adjacent functions through institutions rather than personalists. | `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.4` |
| E4 | Favorable / institutional response | [Philippine VP’s death threat against president a security matter, official says](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippine-vps-death-threat-against-president-a-national-security-matter-official-says-3738424) — Reuters, Nov. 23, 2024 | After the assassination threat, the security council said it would verify the threat and work with law enforcement and intelligence communities. That is evidence of reliance on formal risk-assessment and protective institutions in a high-stress situation. | `1B.7`, `1B.3` |
| E5 | Mixed / limiting context | [PBBM reorganizes NSC, removes VP, ex-presidents as members](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2021249/marcos-drops-sara-former-presidents-in-nsc-revamp) — Inquirer, Jan. 3, 2025, describing EO 81 signed Dec. 30, 2024 | The reorganization also narrowed membership by removing the vice president and former presidents. That can be read as reducing political drag, but it also centralizes discretion in the president because EO 81 lets him appoint “other government officials and private citizens” as needed. | `1B.7` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 1B.7:** The NSC was explicitly framed as a **technical, permanent advisory institution**, and Marcos’s 2024 reorganization reinforced that structure with cabinet, legislative, intelligence, military, and legal participants.
- **Best limiting evidence:** The President retains broad appointment discretion, so the structure still depends on his choices. The available record does **not** let me verify how many of those appointees were neutral experts versus political loyalists.
- **Search gap:** I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that Marcos surrounded nuclear/security decisions with ideologues, nor any clear case of him bypassing institutions in favor of personal loyalists. The available evidence supports **institutionalization**, but only at a structural level.

**Working judgment for 1B.7:** **Mostly yes.** Marcos appears to have leaned on **formal institutions and security professionals** in 2024, though the record is not strong enough to prove deep technocratic insulation from political influence.
